tia_content.bandwidth: 'around 124 MHz in this case, assuming GBWP = 1.5 GHz, C_CM (LMH6624 CM input capacitance) = 0.9 pF, and C_DIFF (LMH6624 DIFF input capacitance) = 2 pF' (Eq 9)
tia_content.other: +5 V single supply; IN+ biased at 3 V by 2 k (to +5 V) / 3 k || 0.1 uF; RL = 500 ohm; Vout = 3 VDC - 1200 x I_D. Eq 8: C_F = sqrt(C_IN / (2 pi GBWP R_F)); Eq 9: f_-3dB ~ sqrt(GBWP / (2 pi R_F C_IN)); 'This C_F value is a starting point and C_F needs to be tuned for the particular application as it is often less than 1 pF and thus is easily affected by board parasitics.' DERIVED check: C_IN = 10 + 0.9 + 2 = 12.9 pF, f_-3dB = sqrt(1.5e9 / (2 pi x 1200 x 12.9e-12)) = 124 MHz, C_F = sqrt(12.9e-12 / (2 pi x 1.5e9 x 1200)) = 1.07 pF, matching the text.

tia_content.what: Fig 58 noise gain and transfer function sketch
tia_content.other: NG = (1 + s R_F (C_IN + C_F)) / (1 + s R_F C_F); f_Z ~ 1/(2 pi R_F C_IN); f_P = 1/(2 pi R_F C_F); high-frequency NG = 1 + C_IN/C_F.

tia_content.what: Current noise vs R_F (Eq 10; Fig 59 and Fig 61 'Current Noise Density vs. Feedback Resistance'; Fig 60 equivalent input source model)
tia_content.C_D_or_source_C: C_D = 10 pF drawn, not included in the noise
tia_content.other: Eq 10: i_ni = sqrt(i_n^2 + (e_n/R_F)^2 + 4kT/R_F). Fig 61 (CURVE, vector): total i_ni 4.74 pA/rtHz at 1 kohm, 4.02 at 1.5 kohm, 3.65 at 2 kohm; components at 1.5 kohm: thermal 3.29, e_n/R_F 0.58, i_n line 2.26. Fig 59 is numerically identical to LMH6629 Fig 62 (i_n line at 2.60 pA/rtHz, e_n/R_F = 6.85 pA/rtHz at 100 ohm, i.e. e_n = 0.69 nV/rtHz) and therefore shows LMH6629 parameters, not LMH6624. Text p25: 'for R_F < 3 kohm, the noise performance is entirely dominated by R_F thermal noise ... at no R_F setting does the LMH6624 input noise voltage play a significant role. This noise analysis has ignored the possible noise gain increase, due to photo-diode capacitance, at higher frequencies.'

application_guidance: Bias-current cancellation: Rf = Av Rseq, Rg = Rf/(Av - 1) (Eq 1, 2); inverting: Rb on +IN equal to Rf || (Rg + Rs), no less than 25 ohm, optionally shunted by a capacitor; isolate +IN from a 0-ohm source with at least 25 ohm (p17).

Noise model (p18-p19, Eq 3, 4, Fig 51): e_ni dominated by e_n below Rseq = 26 ohm, by resistor thermal noise from 26 ohm to 3.1 kohm, by i_n above 3.1 kohm; e_n and i_n contributions equal at Rseq = 283 ohm. Example: Av = +20, -3 dB 90 MHz, Rseq = 25 ohm -> e_ni = 1.3 nV/rtHz, output noise 309 uVrms. Noise figure Eq 5-7 (p20).
Other examples: deBoo integrator (Fig 52), Sallen-Key low-pass (Fig 53), magnetic-media equalizer with simulated response (Figs 54, 55), single-supply operation with AC coupling (Fig 56) (p20-p22).

Power supply (p26): single or dual supplies 'as long as the input CM voltage range (CMIR) has the required headroom to either supply rail'; low-inductance ceramic decoupling less than 0.5 inch from the pins; ground plane, removed near sensitive pins such as the inputs.

Layout (p26-p27): chip capacitors 1000 pF to 0.1 uF at each supply pin plus 4.7-10 uF tantalum; keep feedback and gain resistor traces short; terminate traces longer than 1 inch; keep resistor values low; EVM layouts Figs 62, 63 place RF and RG on the board bottom 'to minimize summing junction parasitics by reducing trace length'.
abs_max_and_input_protection: Differential input voltage +-1.2 V; supply (V+ - V-) 13.2 V; voltage at input pins V+ + 0.5 V to V- - 0.5 V; input current +-10 mA; soldering 235 C IR (20 s), 260 C wave (10 s); junction 150 C; storage -65 to 150 C (p4 6.1). ESD: HBM +-2000 V (1.5 kohm / 100 pF), machine model +-200 V (p4 6.2). Operating -40 to +125 C. Input clamp structure not described; the +-1.2 V differential limit matters for TIA overload.
other_notes: GBW inconsistency: Features and the TIA text use 1.5 GHz, closed-loop high-gain data (Fig 6) give 1.4-1.7 GHz, but the open-loop plots (Figs 7, 8) give |A_OL| about 41 dB at 10 MHz and 20 dB at 100 MHz, i.e. 1.0-1.15 GHz, with the unity-gain crossover at about 0.5 GHz.
Noise curves Figs 1 and 2 plot about 1.0 nV/rtHz and 1.8-1.9 pA/rtHz flat to 10 MHz, which match the LMH6626 table values (1.0, 1.8) rather than the LMH6624 values (0.92, 2.3).
Fig 59 (p25) reproduces the LMH6629 TIA-noise plot (0.69 nV/rtHz, 2.6 pA/rtHz); Fig 61 on the same page is the LMH6624 version (i_n 2.26 pA/rtHz, e_n about 0.89 nV/rtHz).
Description quotes 100 uV VOS and +-0.1 uV/C drift; the tables give +-0.10 mV TYP and +-0.2 uV/C (+-6 V), -0.25 mV and +-0.25 uV/C (+-2.5 V).
Input capacitances (0.9 pF CM, 2.0 pF DIFF) are simulation values.
The input common-mode range is given only as CMRR test conditions and does not reach V- (1.5-2 V headroom needed); single-supply TIA examples bias +IN at 3 V on 5 V.
